description: Participants compute each idea of linear algebra twice: by hand on small cases and in array code on real data. They treat data as vectors, matrices as transformations, least squares as projection, and eigen and singular value decompositions as ways to find structure. Labs use public embeddings and images and a synthetic link graph. The capstone is a low-rank analysis of a public dataset, defended orally.
audience: Beginners. Career changers and non-computing graduates closing bridging gaps before advanced study, and computing graduates refreshing the mathematics behind models; a placement test lets participants skip any course whose content they already command.
prerequisites: School algebra: solving equations and reading graphs of functions
Writes short Python programs with lists, loops and functions (FND-PRG-101 or equivalent)

outcomes.text: Explain the geometric meaning of vectors, dot products, norms, projections and matrix products, given two- and three-dimensional examples
outcomes.evidence: supervised AI-off test, at least 70% correct

outcomes.text: Describe what rank, eigenvalues and singular values reveal about a matrix and name one machine learning use of each, given covariance and data matrices
outcomes.evidence: written answers marked against a rubric

outcomes.text: Identify ill-conditioned or rank-deficient systems and explain their effect on a least-squares fit, given five numerical cases
outcomes.evidence: a diagnosis sheet correct on four of five

outcomes.text: Compute products, inverses, projections and decompositions by hand for small matrices and in array code for large ones, given the weekly problem sets
outcomes.evidence: notebooks in which hand and code results agree within tolerance

outcomes.text: Implement least squares through QR factorisation and compare it with the normal equations, given synthetic data with nearly collinear features
outcomes.evidence: a notebook comparing residuals and condition numbers, with the difference explained

outcomes.text: Apply the singular value decomposition to build low-rank approximations and principal components, given a public image, ratings or embedding matrix
outcomes.evidence: the capstone notebook with error by rank and an interpretation of the leading components
